relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: Rouse was sent to Regent's Park College in London, where he studied as a lay student.

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: In 1881, he won a scholarship to Christ's College, Cambridge.

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: He achieved a double first in the Classical Tripos at the University of Cambridge, where he also studied Sanskrit.

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: He became a Fellow of Christ's College in 1888

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: later received the degree Doctor in Letters from the college in early 1903.

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: After brief spells at Bedford School (1886–1888)

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: Rouse became a master at Rugby School

relations.subject: Arthur Ransome
relations.evidence: Rouse became a master at Rugby School, where he encouraged Arthur Ransome to become a writer... 'I came at once into the hands of a most remarkable man whom I might otherwise never have met. This was Dr W. H. D. Rouse.'

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.evidence: Rouse was appointed headmaster of The Perse School in Cambridge in 1902... He retired from teaching in 1928.

relations.subject: William Henry Denham Rouse
relations.role: founding editors of the Loeb Classical Library
relations.evidence: The same year, James Loeb chose W.H.D. Rouse, together with two other eminent classical scholars, T. E. Page and Edward Capps, to be founding editors of the Loeb Classical Library.
